text:
Anya: Quick heads-up — hit an ambiguous model-selection case in gateway tests. Client sent both an explicit version tag and an alias; gateway picked the alias mapping unexpectedly. Repro below.

Jeff: Can you paste the exact headers you sent?

Anya: Sure:
```
POST /v1/generate
Host: api.redwood.dev
Authorization: Bearer ...
X-Model: redwood/gpt-neo
X-Model-Alias: enterprise/sales-llm
Content-Type: application/json
```
Body is a tiny prompt. Alias `enterprise/sales-llm` is mapped to `redwood/gpt-neo:v2` in the catalog, but gateway routed to `redwood/gpt-neo:v1`.

Marta: That's surprising — what's our intended precedence right now? I thought explicit header (X-Model) should win if it contains a version, and alias when it's just a family.

Anya: Exactly, but in this case `X-Model` had no `:vN` suffix, so gateway treated it as "family" and then applied alias resolution which has its own version pin. The tie-break logic is: route-rule tags -> alias resolution -> explicit family -> default. That ordering is what caused v1 to be selected.

Sanjay: Hmm privacy/telemetry question: how are we recording the decision? We log which rule matched, but not the full headers because of PII concerns. If we change precedence we need telemetry that still lets us debug mismatches without leaking header values to logs.

Jeff: Proposal: make precedence deterministic and intuitive: 1) explicit model with version (e.g., `redwood/gpt:v2`) 2) explicit model family without version (treat as family) 3) alias mapping (alias may pin to a version) 4) route-based pin/fallback. Also add a decision trace token in responses and internal telemetry (not user-visible) that says which source decided. Example response header: `X-RW-Route-Decision: resolved_by=alias;alias=enterprise/sales-llm;matched_rule=tenant-prefix` (redacted in user-facing logs).

Marta: UX idea for Console: show a per-request "routing trace" panel when you click a request in traces (only visible to customer admins and our ops), with fields: matched_rule, alias_resolution, final_model_id. That will cut down support back-and-forth.

Anya: +1. Also want a small gateway config change: if client provides both `X-Model` family and `X-Model-Alias`, prefer the more specific pin (i.e., if alias pins v2 and family explicitly says v1, we must respect explicit version tag). So explicit version tag should always override alias.

Sanjay: Sound safe, but please ensure we don't expose alias content in logs. Telemetry metric names can be enum'd: `routing.source={explicit_version,explicit_family,alias,route_default}`. Counts only.

Jeff: Implementation plan: add unit tests for combinations (explicit family vs alias vs explicit version), add an integration canary, and emit `routing.source` tag to metrics + an internal-only `route_trace_id` that links to a privacy-safe trace blob.

deploy-bot: Canary deployed: gateway/resolve-precedence v2 -> tests passed on canary (10% traffic). Link: https://ci.redwood.dev/ci/3872

Marta: Nice. Can we also add a console guardrail: when a route rule and alias disagree on pinned version, show a warning on alias edit flow? A small UX nudge will save support churn.

Anya: Agree. I'll open a PR that enforces explicit-version precedence, adds the `routing.source` metric, and wires a minimal trace id to internal logging. Will add a docs blurb for the Console team.

Jeff: Thanks — once PR is up ping here and we'll coordinate a staged rollout. :thumbsup: 

Sanjay: If possible make the trace id opt-in at org level for privacy-conscious customers.

Anya: Good call. I'll add an org-level toggle with default off.

deploy-bot: CI green on PR #4127. Ready for review.

Jeff: Reviewing now. If all good we'll merge and expand canary to 50%.
